plain_statement: Assume the free-input chain law: in every minimal circuit of x OR H, H non-constant and free of x, the gates above x form a chain of OR gates up to the output. Let C be a fan-in-two circuit on n + 1 inputs whose input e (not the last input q) is read only by a NOT gate, that gate only by an AND gate, that AND gate only by an OR gate; suppose C with x_e set to 1 computes x_q OR H, H non-constant, and C is false where only x_q is 1. Then C with x_e set to 1 has a circuit of |C| - 4 gates, and of |C| - 5 if the AND gate also lists a gate other than the NOT gate that only it reads.
title: NOT state at an input read only through a NOT, then an AND, then an OR: fixing it to 1 saves four gates, five when the AND has a private gate operand
